subject: Network hardening and traffic controls for Peregrine Health — Dedicated/Private deployment narrative
messages:
From: Mark Jenkins <mark.jenkins@peregrinehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@peregrinehealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood network boundaries for Dedicated/Private — request for architecture narrative

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As part of our SOC 2 readiness and SIG review, our security team has asked for a short architecture narrative that explains how Redwood separates customer traffic and control-plane signals for Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically we need:

- A network diagram that shows perimeter, control plane, and model-serving enclaves for both Dedicated and Private (VPC/VPN) modes.
- How egress is controlled / audited (per-tenant egress rules, NAT vs. proxy, logging).
- Where keys are stored (KMS/HSM boundaries) and any shared-service access patterns.
- A short statement of how failover works if a dedicated pool loses capacity and whether fallback invokes hosted models.

Can you share a narrative + diagram and any evidence matrix mapping to SIG/CAT/CaIQ questions? We don’t need full SOC 2 artifacts yet — just the architecture-level narrative and artifacts we can attach to the SIG questionnaire.

Thanks,
Mark
Mark Jenkins
Head of InfoSec, Peregrine Health
mark.jenkins@peregrinehealth.com

Subject: Re: Redwood network boundaries for Dedicated/Private — request for architecture narrative

Hi Mark — thanks, and great question.

Attached: segmentation_diagram_v1.png (high-level), layered_evidence_matrix.csv (SIG mapping), redwood-dsa-draft.pdf (draft DSA for review).

Summary (high level):
- Zones: Perimeter (ingress LB + WAF), Customer Edge/VPN (for Private), Tenant Enclave (model serving), Control Plane (centralized but isolated), Shared Services (observability, artifact storage).
- Dedicated: Customers are provisioned onto a dedicated GPU pool (tenant enclave) that is reachable only via a customer-dedicated VPC peering or private interconnect. Control-plane signals (scheduling, telemetry) are sent over mutually authenticated mTLS channels to a control-plane subnet that does not have direct access to tenant storage.
- Private (VPC-hosted): We deploy a customer-specific control-plane proxy inside their VPC that forwards only authenticated control messages; model-serving runs inside their private VPC with optional air-gapped storage.
- Egress & auditing: All outbound connections from tenant enclaves are subject to per-tenant egress ACLs enforced by our egress proxy (mutually authenticated) and logged via an immutable audit stream. We retain tokenized flow logs for 90 days by default (configurable).
- Key boundaries: Customer encryption keys may be customer-managed (bring-your-own-key) in their KMS/HSM. Redwood's control plane stores only ephemeral wrapping keys; persistent model artifacts can be encrypted with customer keys when configured.
- Failover: For Dedicated pools, our routing policy supports automatic fallbacks to either (a) a compatible dedicated pool in another AZ/region or (b) a hosted model variant if the customer authorizes fallback. Fallback decisions are governed by configured rollout policies and are logged with reason codes for audit.

Next steps: Kimberly will add the network ACL and routing rules mapping; Karthik will annotate the SIG/CaIQ rows in the evidence matrix. If you can confirm which SIG version you need (v2026 vs v2027) we’ll prioritize that mapping.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Solutions Engineering

On Mon, May 31, 2027 at 10:04 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Attached: segmentation_diagram_v1.png (high-level), layered_evidence_matrix.csv (SIG mapping), redwood-dsa-draft.pdf (draft DSA for review).

Hi Mark — adding the technical controls you asked for, annotated to the attached diagram. Short bullets for the SIG rows you highlighted: 

- Per-tenant isolation: Tenant enclaves are implemented using dedicated VPC subnets and strict security group rules. No cross-tenant routing is permitted inside the model-serving layer.
- Control-plane separation: Control-plane hosts are in a separate VPC with a one-way communication pattern for scheduling signals (control-plane -> tenant via mutually authenticated tunnels). The control-plane cannot initiate direct S3/API calls into tenant storage buckets — any such operation must be mediated by tenant-authorized proxies.
- Egress enforcement: Egress flows are forced through our egress proxy which enforces policy by tenant, performs TLS interception only for outbound metadata (for logging) and forwards TLS payloads unchanged when configured. Egress proxy instances are placed in an isolated subnet with route tables that only allow explicit NAT or proxy routes.
- Network ACLs & firewall rules: We use explicit deny-by-default firewall policies at the subnet boundary. Per-tenant ACLs are generated from the tenant config and pushed via our infra pipeline; changes are auditable and require CI/CD approval.
- Key management: When BYOK is enabled, customer KMS keys remain in customer-controlled accounts; Redwood stores only key identifiers and short-lived wrapped keys. For Redwood-managed keys we use HSM-backed KMS with strict separation between control-plane and serving-plane key access roles.
- Logging & retention: VPC Flow logs + egress proxy logs are aggregated to an immutable audit service. SIG-relevant logs (authentication, routing changes, egress decisions) are retained for 365 days for enterprise customers.

Attachments referenced in the diagram:
- segmentation_diagram_v1.png (zone legend + CIDR ranges redacted)
- layered_evidence_matrix.csv (SIG -> evidence file mapping)

If helpful we can provide a sanitized network table with example CIDR allocations and example iptables/nft rules.

Thanks,
